questions.prompt: Which actions reduce the spread of flu in a classroom? Choose all that apply.
In the Germ Spread Classroom, why did we compare averages over 60 outbreaks?
options: Chance affects each single outbreak, so averages give a fairer comparison
questions.explain: Repeating trials reduces the effect of chance.

questions.prompt: Without any measures, an average of 23 pupils caught flu. With all measures, the average was 2. By what percentage did the measures cut cases (to the nearest whole number)?
Why does opening windows help reduce the spread of airborne diseases?
options: Fresh air dilutes and carries away tiny droplets containing germs
questions.explain: Ventilation lowers the concentration of germs in the air.

questions.prompt: The Swachh Bharat Mission built millions of toilets across India. Which diseases does this especially help prevent?
options: Diseases spread through water and food contaminated by faeces, like diarrhoea and typhoid
questions.explain: Sanitation keeps faeces out of water and food.

questions.prompt: Your school wants to reduce illness during the flu season. Design a plan with three measures and evaluate one limitation of each.
questions.modelAnswer: 1) Handwashing stations with soap near classrooms and canteens: effective, but pupils may skip washing, so reminders and time are needed. 2) Keep windows open and use fans for ventilation: cheap, but hard in very cold or rainy weather. 3) Ask pupils with fever or cough to rest at home, with homework shared online: reduces spread, but families with working parents may find it hard, and pupils might miss lessons. Also encourage flu vaccination for vulnerable people.
questions.explain: Criterion D: evaluate a real plan.

questions.prompt: Order the steps for washing hands properly.
steps: Scrub all surfaces, including between fingers and under nails, for 20 seconds
questions.explain: Scrubbing for 20 seconds is the key step.

questions.text: Keeping our surroundings and bodies clean to prevent disease is called ___.
questions.explain: Personal and community hygiene both matter.
